structured.approach: I followed the DS-01 procedure in the data-science-steps skill. From feat.tasks I took the Data Science lane's tasks (TSK-03 and TSK-04, both in ap_forecast). From org.engineering_stack I took the language, CI command, coverage bar and branch convention, and the statement that no repository uses Databricks or a database. Step policy (G9) blocks shell commands in DS-01, so my git commands were refused. Instead I relied on the spine's tool:repo-access view for availability, the branch and write access. I backed it up by reading files in the checkout: .git/HEAD and refs/heads, __init__.py for the version and exports, ci.py for the CI gate, and the source and test layout. I wrote task.repo_access.md with the outcome. It also lists two non-blocking questions: whether the coverage package is installed on the runner, and whether the single branch feature/story is right for two stories.
tools_used: Bash (attempted; denied by G9 hook for DS-01)

claims.text: The Data Science lane owns TSK-03 (STORY-03, vendor_risk) and TSK-04 (STORY-04, risk parameter on build_explanation_request), both in repository ap_forecast.
ap_forecast is Python 3.9 with unittest, its CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py, and every CI enforces line coverage >= 90%.
Repository ap_forecast is available locally. Branch feature/story was created from dev at d67e866, and the agent identity has write access (git status clean).
No repository creation is needed, and no Databricks, other workspace or database is used by ap_forecast.
The checkout HEAD points to refs/heads/feature/story, and the branches main, dev and feature/story exist.
The current package version is 0.9.0, with __all__ exporting predict_delay_days and build_explanation_request.

ci.py checks compilation, runs the unit tests, requires coverage of at least COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0, and flags print, eval and exec, bare except, and lines longer than 140 characters. It imports the coverage package.
TSK-03 owns the ap_forecast version step from 0.9.0 and adds tests/test_risk.py; TSK-04 extends tests/test_forecast.py.
Commit messages start with the story ID.

open_questions: RAQ-1: Is the coverage package that ci.py imports installed for /usr/bin/python3 on the runner? This step could not run CI to confirm. Interim answer: assume yes; the first CI run in DS-05/DS-06 confirms.

RAQ-2: The convention is feature/<story>, but this lane has two stories (STORY-03 and STORY-04) and was given the single branch feature/story. Should they get separate branches? Interim answer: use feature/story for both, with story-prefixed commits.
structured.summary: The DS-01 outcome is met. ap_forecast, the only repository the Data Science lane needs for TSK-03 and TSK-04, is available locally with write access on feature/story (from dev at d67e866). No repository creation and no Databricks or database access are needed. task.repo_access.md records availability, branches, the current version (0.9.0), the CI gate (coverage >= 90, static checks) and the commit convention. It also has two non-blocking questions: whether coverage is installed on the runner, and whether one branch for two stories is acceptable. Shell commands were blocked for this step, so I ran no git or CI commands; the access facts come from the spine's tool view and the checkout files.

tool_input.command: git status --short --branch && git branch -a && git log --oneline -3 --all && git remote -v; ls; ls src/ap_forecast tests; grep -n "__version__" src/ap_forecast/__init__.py; test -w . && echo writable
tool_input.description: Inspect ap_forecast repo branches, remote and layout
Show ap_forecast branch and working tree status
